The sonne of man in earth.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Priests do remit sinnes.}}By which act ({{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''In catena S. Thomæ''.}}saith S. Cyril) it is cleere that the Sonne of man hath power in earth to remit sinnes: which he said both for him self and vs. For he, as God being made man and Lord of the Law, forgiueth sinnes. And we also haue obtained by him that wonderful grace. for it is said to his Disciples, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 20, 23.''}}''Whose sinnes you shal remit, they are remitted to them''. And how should not he be able to remit sinnes, Who gaue others power to doe the same?

''28. Leauing al folowed him.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Forsaking al, and folovving Christ.}}The {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Hiero. in Mt. 9.''}}profane Iulian charged Matthevv of to much lightnes, to leaue al and folovv a stranger, at one vvord. but in deede hereby is seen the maruelous efficacie of Christes vvord and internal vvorking, that in a moment can alter the hart of a man, and cause him nothing to esteeme the things most deere vnto him. Which he did not onely then in presence, but also daily doth in the Church. For so S. Antonie, S. Francis, and others, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Athan. in vit. S. Antonij. August. confes. li. 8 c. 12. Bonau. in vit. S. Francisci''.}}by hearing only the word of our Sauiour read in the Church, forsooke al and folowed him.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. VI.}}}}}}

{{c|''For reprouing by Scripture and miracle (as also by reason) the Pharisees blindnes about the obseruation of the Sabboth, 11. they seeke his death. 12. Hauing in the mountaine prayed al night, he chooseth twelue Apostles. 17. and after many miracles vpon the diseased, 20. he maketh a sermon to his Disciples before the people: proposing heauen to such as wil suffer for him, 24. and wo to such as vvil not. 27. Yet vvithal exhorting to doe good euen to our enemies also. 19. and that the Maisters must first mend them selues. 46. finally, to doe good vvorkes, because only faith vvil not suffice.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=6|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 12, 1. Mr. 2, 23.''}}* it came to passe on the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Hierom (ep. 2 ad Nepotian.) writeth of him self, that being at Constantinople, he asked his maister Gregorie Nazianzene, the famous Doctor, then Bishop there, what Sabboth this was. who by his answer declared that it was very hard to tel, neither is it yet knowen to the best learned. Yet the Protestants are wont to say, Al is very easie.}}∷ Sabboth second-first, vvhen he passed through the corne, his Disciples did plucke the eares, and did eate rubbing them vvith their hands. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=2}}† And certaine of the Pharisees said to them, VVhy doe you that vvhich is not lawful on the Sabboths? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=3}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering them, said, {{sup|‖}} Neither this haue you read vvhich Dauid did, vvhen him self vvas an hungred and they that vvere vvith him: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=4}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Re. 21, 4.''}}* hovv he entred into the house of God, and tooke the loaues of Proposition, and did eate, and gaue to them that vvere vvith him, vvhich it is not lavvful to eate {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 24, 9.''}}* but only for Priests? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=5}}† And he said to them, That the sonne of man is Lord of the Sabboth also.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=6}}† And it came to passe on an other Sabboth also, that he entred into the synagogue, and taught. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 12, 10. Mr. 3, 1.''}}* And there vvas a man, and his right hand vvas vvithered. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=7}}† And the Scribes and Pharisees vvatched if he vvould cure on the Sabboth: that they might finde hovv to accuse him. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=8}}† But he knevv their cogitations: and he said to the man that had the withered hand, Arise, and stand forth into the middes. And rising he stoode. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=9}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, I aske you, if it be lavvful on the Sabboths to doe vvel or il: to {{sup|‖}} saue a soule or to destroy? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=10}}† And looking about vpon them al, he said to the<noinclude>{{rh|||man,}}</noinclude>
